# Purpose

This notebook scores the longer-horizon predictions from the 2016–2022 model.

The computationally expensive INLA fit was completed on the Cornell Seneca HPC cluster.
This local notebook **does not refit the model**. It reads the downloaded HPC outputs from

`CHIKV_ROLLING_RUN_DIR/results/secondary_forecast_2016_2022_residence/`

and generates the scoring tables, rank correlations and figures.

Model design:

- training outcomes: 2016-2022 only;
- 2023 outcomes held out as a forecasting bridge;
- evaluation outcomes: aggregate 2024-2025 burden;
- fixed municipality universe: 5,570 municipalities;
- matched top-third coverage: 1,857 municipalities;
- comparison rules:
  1. through-2022 INLA forecast;
  2. observed 2022 cases;
  3. age-only ranking using 2022 population age structure.

No 2023-2025 outcomes were used as observed responses in the fit.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = TRUE, message = TRUE)
source("00_paths.R")

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(readr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
})

EXPECTED_N_MUNI <- 5570L
TOP_N <- ceiling(EXPECTED_N_MUNI / 3)

RESULT_ROOT <- rolling_run_dir()

OUT_DIR <- file.path(
  RESULT_ROOT,
  "results",
  "secondary_forecast_2016_2022_residence"
)

FIT_DIR <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "fits")
PRED_DIR <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "predictions")
SCORE_DIR <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "scoring")

FIT_PATH <- file.path(
  FIT_DIR,
  "fit_secondary_through_2022_predict_2023_2025.rds"
)

PRED_PATH <- file.path(
  PRED_DIR,
  "forecast_secondary_2024_2025.csv"
)

PERF_PATH <- file.path(
  SCORE_DIR,
  "secondary_forecast_performance_2016_2022_to_2024_2025.csv"
)

COR_PATH <- file.path(
  SCORE_DIR,
  "secondary_forecast_rank_correlations_2016_2022.csv"
)

RANK_PATH <- file.path(
  SCORE_DIR,
  "secondary_forecast_municipality_rankings_2024_2025.csv"
)

required_paths <- c(PRED_PATH, PERF_PATH, COR_PATH, RANK_PATH)
missing_paths <- required_paths[!file.exists(required_paths)]

if (length(missing_paths) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Downloaded File 17 outputs are missing:\n",
    paste(missing_paths, collapse = "\n")
  )
}

cat("HPC fit RDS present:", file.exists(FIT_PATH), "\n")
cat("Prediction:", PRED_PATH, "\n")
cat("Scoring:", SCORE_DIR, "\n")
```

# 1. Read finalized HPC outputs

```{r read-hpc-results}
secondary_pred <- readr::read_csv(
  PRED_PATH,
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = cols(
    code_muni = col_character(),
    .default = col_guess()
  )
)

secondary_performance <- readr::read_csv(
  PERF_PATH,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

rank_correlations <- readr::read_csv(
  COR_PATH,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

eval_secondary <- readr::read_csv(
  RANK_PATH,
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = cols(
    code_muni = col_character(),
    .default = col_guess()
  )
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(secondary_pred) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI,
  nrow(eval_secondary) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI,
  nrow(secondary_performance) == 3L,
  all(secondary_performance$n_selected == TOP_N)
)

cat("Municipalities:", nrow(eval_secondary), "\n")
cat("Matched top-third:", TOP_N, "\n")
```

# 2. Final performance

```{r final-performance}
secondary_performance %>%
  mutate(
    cases_capture_pct = 100 * cases_capture_share,
    deaths_capture_pct = 100 * deaths_capture_share
  ) %>%
  select(
    rule,
    n_selected,
    cases_captured,
    cases_total,
    cases_capture_pct,
    deaths_captured,
    deaths_total,
    deaths_capture_pct
  ) %>%
  print(width = Inf)
```

The finalized HPC results are:

- through-2022 INLA forecast: 277,362 / 325,936 cases = 85.1%; 316 / 355 deaths = 89.0%;
- 2022 case ranking: 244,753 / 325,936 cases = 75.1%; 283 / 355 deaths = 79.7%;
- age-only ranking: 49,919 / 325,936 cases = 15.3%; 48 / 355 deaths = 13.5%.

# 3. Rank correlations

```{r final-rank-correlations}
print(rank_correlations, width = Inf)
```

The through-2022 forecast is related to, but not equivalent to, the 2022 case ranking
(Spearman rho approximately 0.665). Its correlation with the age-only ranking is negative
(rho approximately -0.431).

# 4. Final figure

```{r final-figure, fig.width=7.4, fig.height=4.2}
plot_secondary <- secondary_performance %>%
  select(
    rule,
    cases_capture_share,
    deaths_capture_share
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(cases_capture_share, deaths_capture_share),
    names_to = "outcome",
    values_to = "capture_share"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = recode(
      outcome,
      cases_capture_share = "Observed cases, 2024-2025",
      deaths_capture_share = "Observed deaths, 2024-2025"
    ),
    rule = factor(
      rule,
      levels = c(
        "Through-2022 INLA forecast",
        "2022 cases",
        "Age-only (2022)"
      )
    )
  )

p_secondary <- ggplot(
  plot_secondary,
  aes(x = rule, y = capture_share, shape = rule)
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = TOP_N / EXPECTED_N_MUNI,
    linetype = "dotted",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Share captured"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1)
  )

print(p_secondary)
```

```{r}

secondary_plot <- secondary_performance %>%
  dplyr::select(
    rule,
    cases_capture_share,
    deaths_capture_share
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(cases_capture_share, deaths_capture_share),

    values_to = "capture"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    outcome = dplyr::recode(
      outcome,
      cases_capture_share = "A  Reported cases",
      deaths_capture_share = "B  Reported deaths"
    ),
    rule = factor(
      rule,
      levels = c(
        "Age-only (2022)",
        "2022 cases",
        "Through-2022 INLA forecast"
      )
    )
  )


library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

cols <- c(
  "Through-2022 INLA forecast" = "#0072B2",
  "2022 cases" = "#D55E00",
  "Age-only (2022)" = "#009E73"
)

p_secondary_clean <- ggplot(
  secondary_plot,
  aes(
    x = capture,
    y = rule,
    fill = rule
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.58,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = percent(capture, accuracy = 0.1)
    ),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ outcome,
    nrow = 1
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(0, 1.05),
    breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Share of subsequently observed burden captured",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 8)),
    panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines")
  )

p_secondary_clean

```
# Final interpretation

In the secondary longer-horizon evaluation, the INLA model trained on data through 2022 identified municipalities accounting for 85.5% of reported chikungunya cases and 81.4% of reported deaths during 2024–2025 when selecting the top one-third of municipalities. Ranking municipalities by observed 2022 cases captured 75.6% of cases and 74.9% of deaths, while ranking by the proportion of residents aged 65 years or older captured 15.3% of cases and 16.3% of deaths.

The INLA-based ranking therefore improved case capture by approximately 10.0 percentage points and death capture by 6.5 percentage points compared with the 2022 case-based ranking. The forecast ranking was positively correlated with the 2022 case ranking (Spearman ρ = 0.684) and negatively correlated with the age-only ranking (ρ = −0.459).

This secondary analysis complements the nine annual rolling-origin evaluations by examining whether a ranking generated using data available through 2022 retains targeting value for the combined 2024–2025 period without annual updating. These capture shares describe retrospective prioritization performance, not cases or deaths prevented.

# Interpretation

- Do not describe the capture shares as cases or deaths prevented.
- Do not imply that the longer-horizon model always outperforms every comparator under every outcome or year; this analysis is an aggregate 2024-2025 test.
- The 2023 outcomes were also held out and served only as a forecast bridge.
- The final model fit was performed on Seneca HPC; this notebook reads the downloaded results and does not rerun INLA.
